# Neuronetworks AI Ed: full program reference

> Practical AI and technology programs for students who have passed Class 10, from a six-month AI Foundation course to three-year specialisations. Tagline: Learn · Develop · Create. Website: https://neuronetwrks.com. Contact: Hussain@neuronetwrks.com. Fees are shared on enquiry.

## AI Foundation (6 months, 104 hours, 4 hours a week)
URL: https://neuronetwrks.com/programs/ai-foundation

AI Foundation is a six-month, 104-hour course open to students from Class 9, with no prior coding needed. It moves from AI basics and responsible use to real Python, data handling with Pandas, NumPy and Matplotlib, machine learning, computer vision and NLP, generative AI and LLMs, prompt and context engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), Python AI APIs and agents, and building, testing and deploying a complete AI application. The final month covers Microsoft AI-901 and AWS AIF-C01 exam preparation and a capstone project published to GitHub, without promising an exam pass.

Entry: Class 9 and above; no prior coding, AI or cloud experience required.
Assessment: 104 one-hour lectures, each with 10 to 15 minutes of homework. A 30-question unit exam closes every major unit, with mandatory practicals in Module 4 (Python and Pandas data cleaning) and Module 5 (an end-to-end ML practical). Both certification tracks end in a full-length mock exam, and the course closes with a capstone presentation and practical assessment.

- Year 1 (104 hours): AI Foundations & How Modern AI Works (4 h); AI Tools, Safety, Ethics & Responsible AI (4 h); Python Programming Fundamentals I (10 h); Python Programming Fundamentals II & Data Science (8 h); Machine Learning Fundamentals with Python (10 h); Computer Vision, NLP & Multimodal AI (6 h); Generative AI, LLMs & Foundation Models (8 h); Prompt Engineering & AI Evaluation (7 h); Context Engineering, Embeddings & RAG (8 h); Python AI APIs, Agents & Automation (9 h); AI Application Development, Testing & Deployment (12 h); Cloud AI, Final Capstone & Graduation (18 h)

Projects: Practical AI audit; Responsible AI workshop; Debugging and programming challenge; Cleaned-CSV data mini-project on GitHub; ML mini-project and practical assessment; Practical multimodal AI application; Small generative AI application; Prompt evaluation benchmark project; RAG Knowledge Assistant project; AI workflow and agent project; Complete tested and deployed AI application; Final capstone project and graduation

Tools: Python, NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, scikit-learn, Git and GitHub, LLM APIs, Microsoft Foundry, AWS

Certification preparation (awarded by the certifying organisations; passing not guaranteed): Microsoft Azure AI Fundamentals (AI-901); AWS Certified AI Practitioner (AIF-C01)

Completion: students receive a Neuronetworks AI Ed certificate on completing the program. Laptop specifications are recommendations.

FAQs:
- Q: Who is the AI Foundation course for? A: It is open to students from Class 9 upwards, with no prior coding, AI or cloud experience. Students should be able to read simple English instructions, use a browser and manage files.
- Q: How long is the course? A: It is 104 one-hour lectures over 26 weeks (six months), at 4 hours a week. Modules 1 to 11 are core learning (86 hours). The final module has 18 hours: 6 for Microsoft AI-901 preparation, 6 for AWS AIF-C01 preparation and 6 for the final capstone and graduation.
- Q: Will I be certified, and does the course guarantee a pass? A: Students receive a Neuronetworks AI Ed certificate on completing the course. It also prepares students for two optional external exams, Microsoft AI-901 and AWS AIF-C01, but does not guarantee passing; those certifications are awarded by Microsoft or AWS after their exams.
- Q: What will I build? A: A project in almost every module: a data-cleaning mini-project, an ML mini-project, a small generative AI app, a prompt evaluation benchmark, a RAG knowledge assistant, an AI workflow or agent, a complete tested and deployed AI application, and a final capstone published to GitHub.
- Q: Does this make me an AI/ML engineer? A: No. It is a project-based foundation in AI and Python. Students who want depth can continue to a three-year specialisation such as AI/ML Engineering after Class 10.
- Q: What do I need to take part? A: A laptop or desktop with internet and a browser, able to install Python or use a browser-based notebook. A phone alone is not enough for the programming labs. Plan 10 to 15 minutes of homework after each lecture.

## AI/ML Engineering (3 years, 624 hours, 4 hours a week)
URL: https://neuronetwrks.com/programs/ai-ml-engineering

AI/ML Engineering is a three-year, 624-hour specialisation for students who have passed Class 10. It starts with computer and Python basics and builds up to machine learning, deep learning, generative AI and MLOps, with a one-hour exam after each of 36 monthly modules and a project in every month.

Entry: Class 10 pass; basic school-level mathematics and computer familiarity.
Assessment: One 1-hour exam after each of the 36 monthly modules (theory plus practical where appropriate). Exam time is included in the 624 hours.

- Year 1 (208 hours): Computer + AI Foundations; Python Fundamentals; Python for AI; Math for ML I; Math for ML II; Data Preparation; AI Fundamentals + Google AI Essentials; ML Foundations; Model Evaluation + Azure AI; Classical ML; Unsupervised ML; Year-1 AI Capstone + AI-901
- Year 2 (208 hours): Advanced ML + AWS AI Practitioner; Feature Engineering + Explainability; Time Series + Recommendation; ML Systems Foundations; Deep Learning Fundamentals; PyTorch/TensorFlow Practice; Computer Vision; NLP Fundamentals + NVIDIA DLI; Transformers + IBM AI Engineering I; IBM AI Engineering II; MLOps I; MLOps II + Year-2 Capstone
- Year 3 (208 hours): Generative AI Foundations; Embeddings + RAG; Agents + AI Engineering; Fine-Tuning + PEFT; Computer Vision + Multimodal AI; AI Safety + Responsible AI; Cloud AI Engineering; Advanced MLOps + Observability; AI System Design; Real-World AI Product; GitHub + Portfolio Engineering; Final Professional AI/ML Capstone

Projects: AI concept map + Python mini exercises; CLI utility collection; Python data-processing toolkit; Math-for-ML notebook; Statistical experiment notebook; Messy-dataset cleaning project; AI productivity + evaluation project; House-price/regression project; Azure AI mini solution; Customer-risk classifier; Customer segmentation project; Year-1 production-style ML project; AWS AI service architecture project; Explainable ML project; Demand forecasting project; ML inference API; Neural-network from-scratch exercise; Deep-learning classifier; Image classification application; NLP classifier + DLI lab portfolio; Transformer text application; End-to-end AI service; Containerized ML service; Production ML platform prototype; LLM evaluation playground; Document RAG assistant; Tool-using AI agent; Small-model adaptation project; Multimodal document assistant; AI safety test suite; Cloud AI application; Monitored ML/LLM service; AI platform architecture project; End-to-end AI product; Portfolio with 6–10 flagship projects; Final Professional AI/ML Capstone Project

Tools: Python, Git, GitHub, Docker, Linux, NumPy, Pandas, Scikit-learn, PyTorch, TensorFlow, AWS, Azure

Certification preparation (awarded by the certifying organisations; passing not guaranteed): Microsoft Azure AI Fundamentals (AI-901); AWS Certified AI Practitioner (AIF-C01); Google AI Essentials; NVIDIA DLI Fundamentals of Deep Learning; IBM AI Engineering Professional Certificate

Roles the curriculum is designed around (directions, not guarantees): Junior AI/ML Engineer; Junior Machine Learning Engineer; Applied AI Engineer; GenAI Engineer / Developer; Junior Data Scientist; Computer Vision Engineer (Junior); NLP Engineer (Junior); Junior MLOps Engineer; AI Solutions Developer; AI Automation Developer

Indicative India salary (not guaranteed): Fresher ₹5–10 LPA; 1–2 years ₹7–15 LPA; 3–5 years ₹12–25 LPA; 5–8 years ₹20–40 LPA; Senior ₹30–60+ LPA. Indicative 2026 India market ranges from our curriculum research. They are not a promise: pay depends on the employer, city, role, skills, portfolio and, for some employers, a degree. Neuronetworks AI Ed does not guarantee a job, internship or salary.

Completion: students receive a Neuronetworks AI Ed certificate on completing the program. Laptop specifications are recommendations.

FAQs:
- Q: Who can join this program? A: Class 10 pass; basic school-level mathematics and computer familiarity. The program is designed for students entering after Class 10.
- Q: How many hours is the program, and how is it structured? A: It is 624 hours over three years (36 months): 4 hours a week for 52 weeks a year, or 208 hours a year. Each monthly module ends with a one-hour exam, and exam time is counted inside the 624 hours.
- Q: Does the program guarantee a job or internship? A: No. The curriculum aims at job readiness through skills, hands-on practice, a GitHub record and a portfolio, but it does not guarantee an internship, employment or salary.
- Q: Which external certifications does the roadmap include? A: The program prepares students for five external credentials: Microsoft Azure AI Fundamentals (AI-901); AWS Certified AI Practitioner (AIF-C01); Google AI Essentials; NVIDIA DLI Fundamentals of Deep Learning; IBM AI Engineering Professional Certificate. They are awarded by the certifying organisations, not by this program, and passing an external exam is not guaranteed.
- Q: What laptop do students need? A: Recommended laptop specifications (recommendations, not entry requirements): CPU: Intel i5 / Ryzen 5 or better; RAM: 16 GB minimum, 32 GB recommended; Storage: 512 GB SSD minimum, 1 TB recommended; GPU: Integrated GPU for basic ML; NVIDIA RTX 4060 8 GB+ recommended for the full roadmap; OS: Windows 11 + WSL2 or Linux.
- Q: What kinds of roles does this program prepare students for? A: The curriculum lists entry-level roles such as Junior AI/ML Engineer, Junior Machine Learning Engineer, Applied AI Engineer, GenAI Engineer / Developer. Fit depends on the student's portfolio and on each employer's requirements.

## Software Development (3 years, 624 hours, 4 hours a week)
URL: https://neuronetwrks.com/programs/software-development

The Software Development program is a three-year, 624-hour specialisation for students who have passed Class 10, with no programming knowledge assumed. It progresses from computer and programming fundamentals to professional full-stack, cloud and software-engineering capability, with a one-hour exam after each of 36 monthly modules.

Entry: Class 10 pass; no programming knowledge assumed.
Assessment: One 1-hour exam after each of the 36 monthly modules (theory plus practical where appropriate). Exam time is included in the 624 hours.

- Year 1 (208 hours): Computer & Software Foundations; Programming Logic & Problem Solving; Java Fundamentals I; Java Fundamentals II & OOP; Git, GitHub & Software Collaboration; HTML & Web Fundamentals; CSS & Responsive Design; JavaScript Fundamentals; JavaScript Advanced & APIs; SQL & Relational Databases; Frontend Development with React; Year-1 Full Web Project & AZ-900 Readiness

- Year 3 (208 hours): System Design I; System Design II & Distributed Systems; Cloud-Native Application Engineering; Performance, Scalability & Reliability; Application Security; AI-Assisted Software Development; Advanced Full-Stack Engineering; Software Engineering Practices; AWS Developer Associate Deep Practice; Meta Front-End Portfolio Mastery; Final Engineering Portfolio & Interview Engineering; Final Production Software Capstone

Projects: Personal Developer Setup + First Program Portfolio; 50-Problem Programming Logic Repository; Java CLI Utility Pack; Java OOP Management Application; Collaborative GitHub Project; Personal Developer Website v1; Responsive Portfolio Website; JavaScript Interactive App; API-Driven Web Application; Relational Database Project; React Application v1; Year-1 Full Web Application + GitHub Portfolio Review; DSA Repository I; DSA Repository II; Spring Boot REST API; Java Professional Backend Project; Secure REST API; Hybrid Data Application; Tested Production-Style Application; TypeScript React Application; Full-Stack SaaS Application; AWS-Deployed Application; Containerized CI/CD Project; Year-2 Production SaaS Capstone; System Design Casebook I; Distributed Systems Architecture Project; Cloud-Native Application; Performance Engineering Report; Secure Software Development Project; AI-Assisted Developer Workflow + Audit Report; Major Full-Stack Product v1; Team Software Engineering Simulation; AWS Production Engineering Lab; Professional Front-End Portfolio Project; Developer Portfolio + Interview Challenge Set; Final Production Software Product + Complete GitHub Portfolio

Tools: Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, React, SQL, Git, GitHub, Docker, Linux, Spring Boot, AWS, Azure

Certification preparation (awarded by the certifying organisations; passing not guaranteed): Microsoft Certified: Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900); Oracle Certified Foundations Associate (Java); HackerRank Skills Certification (SQL / Problem Solving); Meta Front-End Developer Professional Certificate; Oracle Certified Professional, Java SE (OCPJP); AWS Certified Developer – Associate

Roles the curriculum is designed around (directions, not guarantees): Junior Software Developer; Junior Software Engineer; Junior Frontend Developer; Junior Backend Developer; Junior Full-Stack Developer; Junior Java Developer; Web Developer; Junior React Developer; Application Developer; Junior Cloud Application Developer; Software QA / Test Automation Trainee; DevOps / Cloud Developer Trainee; Technical Support / Application Support Developer; Freelance Web Developer; Freelance Full-Stack Developer

Indicative India salary (not guaranteed): Fresher ₹4–8 LPA; 1–2 years ₹5–12 LPA; 3–5 years ₹10–20 LPA; 5–8 years ₹18–35 LPA; Senior ₹25–50+ LPA. Indicative 2026 India market ranges from our curriculum research. They are not a promise: pay depends on the employer, city, role, skills, portfolio and, for some employers, a degree. Neuronetworks AI Ed does not guarantee a job, internship or salary.

Completion: students receive a Neuronetworks AI Ed certificate on completing the program. Laptop specifications are recommendations.

FAQs:
- Q: Who can join this program? A: Class 10 pass; no programming knowledge assumed. The program is designed for students entering after Class 10.
- Q: How many hours is the program, and how is it structured? A: It is 624 hours over three years (36 months): 4 hours a week for 52 weeks a year, or 208 hours a year. Each monthly module ends with a one-hour exam, and exam time is counted inside the 624 hours.
- Q: Does the program guarantee a job or internship? A: No. The curriculum aims at job readiness through skills, hands-on practice, a GitHub record and a portfolio, but it does not guarantee an internship, employment or salary.

A: The roadmap lists six external certifications: Microsoft Certified: Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900); Oracle Certified Foundations Associate (Java); HackerRank Skills Certification (SQL / Problem Solving); Meta Front-End Developer Professional Certificate; Oracle Certified Professional, Java SE (OCPJP); AWS Certified Developer – Associate. ## Data Science & AI (3 years, 624 hours, 4 hours a week)
URL: https://neuronetwrks.com/programs/data-science-ai

The Data Science & AI program is a three-year, 624-hour specialisation for Class 10 pass students who are absolute beginners. It progresses from computing, Python, SQL and statistics into analytics, machine learning, data engineering, deep learning, generative AI and MLOps, with a one-hour exam after every monthly module.

Entry: Class 10 pass; absolute beginners welcome.
Assessment: One 1-hour exam after each of the 36 monthly modules (theory plus practical where appropriate). Exam time is included in the 624 hours.

- Year 1 (208 hours): Computer, Data & Python Foundations; Python Programming for Data; SQL Fundamentals; Statistics I; Statistics II; NumPy & Pandas; Data Visualization; Exploratory Data Analysis; Business Analytics; Dashboarding; Google Data Analytics Preparation; Year-1 Capstone & DP-900
- Year 2 (208 hours): Machine Learning Foundations; Feature Engineering & Evaluation; Classification & Ensembles; Unsupervised Learning; Time Series; Data Engineering Foundations; Python Data Engineering; Azure ML & AI-300 Preparation; ML Deployment & MLOps; IBM Data Science Integration; IBM Data Engineering Integration; Year-2 Integrated Capstone
- Year 3 (208 hours): Advanced Machine Learning; Deep Learning; NLP; Computer Vision; Generative AI & RAG; Data Engineering at Scale; Advanced Analytics & Experimentation; Responsible AI; MLOps; Real-World Data Project; GitHub, Portfolio & Interviews; Final Data Science & AI Capstone

Projects: Data Notebook + Python Repository; Python Data Utilities Pack; SQL Analytics Repository; Exploratory Statistics Report; Statistical Investigation; Data Cleaning Notebook Portfolio; Data Storytelling Report; End-to-End EDA Project; Business Analytics Case Study; Analytics Dashboard; Google-Style Analytics Capstone; Year-1 Analytics Capstone; Regression & Classification Project; Model Evaluation Portfolio; Classification System; Segmentation/Anomaly Project; Forecasting Case Study; End-to-End Data Pipeline; Data Ingestion Pipeline; Azure ML Experiment; Production ML API; Data Science Professional Case; Data Engineering Capstone; Production-Style Data Platform; Advanced ML Experiment Suite; Deep Learning Project; NLP Project; Computer Vision Project; RAG Application; Scalable Data Platform; Product Experimentation Case; Responsible AI Audit; MLOps Pipeline; Major End-to-End Data Science Project; Professional Data/AI Portfolio; Final Data Science & AI Capstone

Tools: Python, SQL, Git, GitHub, Linux, NumPy, Pandas, Jupyter, Azure

Certification preparation (awarded by the certifying organisations; passing not guaranteed): Microsoft Certified: Azure Data Fundamentals (DP-900); HackerRank Python & SQL Certificates; Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate; IBM Data Science Professional Certificate; Microsoft AI-300 (Machine Learning Operations Engineer Associate); IBM Data Engineering Professional Certificate

Roles the curriculum is designed around (directions, not guarantees): Junior Data Analyst; Data Analyst; BI Analyst / Junior BI Developer; Junior Data Scientist; Associate Data Scientist; Junior ML Engineer; Junior Data Engineer; Junior Analytics Engineer; ML/AI Analyst; Junior MLOps Engineer; AI/GenAI Data Analyst; Freelance Data Analyst

Indicative India salary (not guaranteed): Fresher ₹4–8 LPA; 1–2 years ₹5–12 LPA; 3–5 years ₹10–22 LPA; 5–8 years ₹18–35 LPA; Senior ₹25–50+ LPA. Indicative 2026 India market ranges from our curriculum research. They are not a promise: pay depends on the employer, city, role, skills, portfolio and, for some employers, a degree. FAQs:
- Q: Who can join this program? A: Class 10 pass; absolute beginners welcome. The program is designed for students entering after Class 10.

## Cybersecurity (3 years, 624 hours, 4 hours a week)
URL: https://neuronetwrks.com/programs/cybersecurity

The Cybersecurity program is a three-year, 624-hour specialisation for students who have passed Class 10, with no technical background assumed. It moves from computers and networking to Linux, security operations and ethical hacking, practised in authorised lab environments, with a one-hour exam after each of 36 monthly modules.

Entry: Class 10 pass; no technical background assumed.
Assessment: One 1-hour exam after each of the 36 monthly modules (theory plus practical where appropriate). Exam time is included in the 624 hours.

- Year 1 (208 hours): Computer & Cybersecurity Foundations; Networking Fundamentals I; Networking Fundamentals II & Subnetting; Linux Fundamentals; Windows & System Administration Fundamentals; Cybersecurity Fundamentals & Security Principles; Identity, Access Control & Cryptography; Security Operations Foundations + ISC2 CC Readiness; Python, Bash & PowerShell for Security; Logs, SIEM & Security Monitoring + Google Certificate; Network Defense: Firewalls, IDS/IPS & Secure Networking; Endpoint Security & Year-1 SOC Project
- Year 2 (208 hours): Threats, Vulnerabilities & Security+ Domain 1; Security Architecture & Design; Security Implementation & Hardening; Security Operations, Incident Response & Security+ Readiness; Vulnerability Management & Security Testing; Ethical Hacking & CEH Foundations; Web Application Security; Network Penetration Testing; Active Directory & Internal Security Testing; Exploitation, Post-Exploitation & Privilege Escalation; CEH Domains, Reporting & Attack Simulation; CEH Capstone + Professional Ethical Hacking Readiness
- Year 3 (208 hours): SOC Engineering & SIEM Architecture; Splunk: Detection, Investigation & Dashboards; Microsoft Sentinel & KQL; Microsoft Defender XDR & Endpoint Investigation; Threat Hunting & MITRE ATT&CK; CySA+ Readiness: Security Operations & Vulnerability Analysis; Incident Response & Digital Forensics; Cloud Security: Azure/AWS Fundamentals & IAM; Cloud Detection, Logging & Security Automation; SC-200 Preparation: Defender, Sentinel & KQL; Advanced Detection Engineering & SOC Simulation; Final Enterprise Cybersecurity Capstone & Job Portfolio

Projects: Cybersecurity concept map + lab notebook + GitHub repository setup; Office Network Diagram + Wireshark Packet Analysis Report; Small Business Network Design + Subnetting Workbook + Troubleshooting Report; Linux Hardening Checklist + Bash Security Toolkit; Windows Security Baseline + PowerShell Audit Script; Mini Enterprise Risk Register + Phishing Investigation Pack; IAM Design + Cryptography Demonstration Report; SOC Starter Playbook + Incident Case File; Security Automation Toolkit v1 (Python + Bash + PowerShell); Mini SOC Dashboard + Brute-Force Investigation Report; Network Defense Lab + IDS Alert Investigation; Year-1 SOC Simulation Project + Portfolio Review; Vulnerability Assessment Report v1; Secure Enterprise Architecture Blueprint; Cross-Platform Hardening Project; Enterprise Incident Response Exercise; Continuous Vulnerability Management Dashboard; Authorized Recon & Enumeration Assessment; Web Application Security Assessment; Internal Network Penetration Test Report; Active Directory Attack-Path & Hardening Project; Red-Team/Blue-Team Privilege Escalation Lab; End-to-End Ethical Hacking Assessment; Year-2 Ethical Hacking Capstone; SOC Architecture & Operations Blueprint; Splunk SOC Investigation Portfolio; Microsoft Sentinel Detection Pack; Defender XDR Incident Investigation Case; Threat Hunting Report + ATT&CK Coverage Matrix; CySA+ Style Analyst Assessment; Digital Forensics Case File + Incident Report; Cloud Security Baseline Assessment; Cloud Detection & Response Automation Project; SC-200 End-to-End Security Operations Lab; Production-Style Detection Engineering Portfolio; Final Enterprise Cybersecurity Defense & Response Capstone

Tools: Python, SQL, Git, GitHub, Linux, Bash, PowerShell, Wireshark, Burp Suite, Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, KQL, AWS, Azure, Suricata

They are awarded by the certifying organisations, not by this program, and passing an external exam is not guaranteed.
- Q: What laptop do students need? A: Recommended laptop specifications (recommendations, not entry requirements): CPU: Intel Core i5 / Ryzen 5 or better; RAM: 16 GB minimum; 32 GB recommended; Storage: 512 GB SSD minimum; 1 TB recommended; GPU: Integrated graphics is sufficient; no dedicated GPU required; Network: Wi-Fi 6 + Gigabit Ethernet preferred.
- Q: What kinds of roles does this program prepare students for? A: The curriculum lists entry-level roles such as SOC Analyst / SOC Analyst L1, Cybersecurity Analyst / Security Analyst, Information Security Analyst, Cyber Defense Analyst. Fit depends on the student's portfolio and on each employer's requirements.

## Notes
- No program guarantees a job, internship, salary or exam pass. Salary figures are indicative market ranges only.
- Certifications are awarded by the certifying organisations, not by Neuronetworks AI Ed.
